title: GA SR789: Senate Study Committee on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence; create

obligations: The committee shall undertake a study of the conditions, needs, issues, and problems mentioned above or related thereto and recommend any action or legislation which the committee deems necessary or appropriate (Sec. 3).
The cochairpersons shall call all meetings of the committee (Sec. 4).
The legislative members of the committee shall receive the allowances provided for in Code Section 28-1-8 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (Sec. 5(A)).

Members of the committee who are state officials, other than legislative members, or who are state employees shall receive no compensation for their services on the committee, but they may be reimbursed for expenses incurred in the performance of their duties in the same manner as they are reimbursed for expenses in their capacities as state officials or employees (Sec. 5(B)).

Members of the committee who are not legislators, state officials, or state employees shall receive a daily expense allowance in an amount the same as that specified in subsection (b) of Code Section 45-7-21 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, as well as the mileage or transportation allowance authorized for state employees (Sec. 5(C)).
The allowances authorized by this resolution shall not be received by any member of the committee for more than five days unless additional days are authorized (Sec. 5(D)).

In the event the committee adopts any specific findings or recommendations that include suggestions for proposed legislation, the cochairpersons shall file a report of the same prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution, subject to subparagraph (C) of this paragraph (Sec. 6(A)).

In the event the committee adopts a report that does not include suggestions for proposed legislation, the cochairpersons shall file the report, subject to subparagraph (C) of this paragraph (Sec. 6(B)).

No report shall be filed unless the same has been approved prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution by majority vote of a quorum of the committee. A report so approved shall be signed by the cochairpersons of the committee and filed with the Secretary of the Senate (Sec. 6(C)).
In the absence of an approved report, the cochairpersons may file with the Secretary of the Senate a copy of the minutes of the meetings of the committee in lieu thereof (Sec. 6(D)).
prohibitions: No report shall be filed unless the same has been approved prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution by majority vote of a quorum of the committee (Sec. 6(C)).
The allowances authorized by this resolution shall not be received by any member of the committee for more than five days unless additional days are authorized (Sec. 5(D)).

What it does

Creates the Senate Study Committee on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Industries. The committee must study conditions, needs, issues, and problems related to artificial intelligence in creative industries and recommend any action or legislation it deems necessary or appropriate.

Who it applies to

  • The Senate Study Committee on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Industries
  • Members of the Senate appointed to the committee
  • Cochairpersons of the committee
  • State officials and state employees serving on the committee
  • Nonlegislator, nonstate official, nonstate employee members of the committee

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • The committee shall undertake a study of the conditions, needs, issues, and problems mentioned above or related thereto and recommend any action or legislation which the committee deems necessary or appropriate (Sec. 3).
  • The cochairpersons shall call all meetings of the committee (Sec. 4).
  • The legislative members of the committee shall receive the allowances provided for in Code Section 28-1-8 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (Sec. 5(A)).
  • Members of the committee who are state officials, other than legislative members, or who are state employees shall receive no compensation for their services on the committee, but they may be reimbursed for expenses incurred in the performance of their duties in the same manner as they are reimbursed for expenses in their capacities as state officials or employees (Sec. 5(B)).
  • Members of the committee who are not legislators, state officials, or state employees shall receive a daily expense allowance in an amount the same as that specified in subsection (b) of Code Section 45-7-21 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, as well as the mileage or transportation allowance authorized for state employees (Sec. 5(C)).
  • The allowances authorized by this resolution shall not be received by any member of the committee for more than five days unless additional days are authorized (Sec. 5(D)).
  • In the event the committee adopts any specific findings or recommendations that include suggestions for proposed legislation, the cochairpersons shall file a report of the same prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution, subject to subparagraph (C) of this paragraph (Sec. 6(A)).
  • In the event the committee adopts a report that does not include suggestions for proposed legislation, the cochairpersons shall file the report, subject to subparagraph (C) of this paragraph (Sec. 6(B)).
  • No report shall be filed unless the same has been approved prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution by majority vote of a quorum of the committee. A report so approved shall be signed by the cochairpersons of the committee and filed with the Secretary of the Senate (Sec. 6(C)).
  • In the absence of an approved report, the cochairpersons may file with the Secretary of the Senate a copy of the minutes of the meetings of the committee in lieu thereof (Sec. 6(D)).

Prohibitions

  • No report shall be filed unless the same has been approved prior to the date of abolishment specified in this resolution by majority vote of a quorum of the committee (Sec. 6(C)).
  • The allowances authorized by this resolution shall not be received by any member of the committee for more than five days unless additional days are authorized (Sec. 5(D)).

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • The resolution does not impose any direct requirements, prohibitions, or penalties on organisations deploying artificial intelligence. It only creates a study committee that may recommend future legislation (Sec. 1, Sec. 3, Sec. 6).
  • Organisations deploying artificial intelligence in creative industries may be affected indirectly if the committee recommends legislation that is later enacted, but no such legislation is created by this resolution (Sec. 3, Sec. 6).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • No compliance steps are required of any organisation deploying artificial intelligence because the resolution only establishes a study committee and imposes no obligations on external parties (Sec. 1 through Sec. 7).
  • For the committee itself, the steps are: the President of the Senate appoints five members and designates two cochairpersons, one from the majority party and one from the minority party (Sec. 2); the cochairpersons call meetings (Sec. 4); the committee undertakes the study and recommends action or legislation (Sec. 3); the committee may adopt a report and the cochairpersons file it with the Secretary of the Senate if approved by majority vote of a quorum (Sec. 6); the committee stands abolished on December 1, 2026 (Sec. 7).

 A RESOLUTION

 3 WHEREAS, artificial intelligence is increasingly used throughout the film and television
 4 industries to automate tasks, impact decision making, and alter audience experiences; and

 6 replacing human artistry and leading to potential job losses for creative writers; and

 8 confusion where handcrafted work is mistaken for artificial intelligence, which can fuel
 9 distrust and controversy, and undisclosed use of artificial intelligence intensifies fears of
10 losing human creativity; and


11 WHEREAS, Georgia has established itself as a national leader for accomplished producers,
12 award-winning actors, and cutting-edge film technology; and
